sections.h2: Where is Clinton, Mississippi, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Clinton is a city in Hinds County, in the Jackson metropolitan area, and the 2020 census counted 28,100 residents, which made it the tenth most populous city in Mississippi. It covers a little over 42 square miles by the 2010 census figures, nearly all of it land.

Three major roads cross the city: Interstate 20, U.S. Route 80, which runs alongside the interstate, and the Natchez Trace Parkway on the west side. Interstate 20 has three exits in the Clinton area, with interchanges at Springridge Road, Clinton-Raymond Road and the Natchez Trace Parkway.

sections.h2: What is Clinton's history, and what does it leave behind?
sections.html:
Clinton was founded in 1823 as Mount Salus, a name meaning mountain of health, and took the name Clinton in 1828 in honor of New York governor DeWitt Clinton. The first road through town was the Natchez Trace, improved from a centuries-old Native American path.

Education has shaped the city for two centuries. Mississippi College, which Wikipedia says became Mississippi Christian University in 2026, was founded in 1826 as Hampstead Academy and is the state's oldest college. Hillman College, founded in 1853 as Central Female Institute, was later incorporated into it.

The city also hosted a World War II prisoner of war camp south of town that held about 3,000 German soldiers. Later it became the headquarters of WorldCom, and Wikipedia calls Clinton the smallest city ever to host a Fortune 500 company. WorldCom was based there from the mid-1990s until 2002. Verizon still occupies the large former WorldCom campus.

sections.h2: What storm and tornado risk should Clinton sellers know about?
sections.html:
Tornadoes are the recorded weather event that stands out in Clinton's history. On April 15, 2011, an EF3 tornado struck around 11:00 a.m., damaged the area near Interstate 20, destroyed the BankPlus building and Malaco Records, and injured ten people.

That single event does not predict the next one, and it also shows why roof condition, window quality and tree trimming matter to buyers and insurers in central Mississippi. Wind damage tends to show up in shingles, flashing, fences and limbs long after a storm.

  • Document the roof's age and any past claims, and keep the paperwork.
  • Photograph repairs before and after so a buyer can see what was done.
  • Trim limbs that overhang the roof, and remove dead trees on the lot.
  • Ask your insurer for a loss history if a buyer requests one.

The city requires permits for construction and related inspections through Community Development, so storm repairs that go beyond patching should be checked with that office first.

sections.h2: How does Clinton's rental inspection ordinance affect a landlord selling a house?
sections.html:
Clinton requires every rental property to be registered, and a rental license is not valid until the unit has passed inspection. The city's ordinance covers manufactured homes, single-family houses, multifamily units and any residential property leased to someone other than the owner.

Key points from the city's description of the program:

  • Any person renting one or more rental units must hold a rental license.
  • Registration is annual for each unit.
  • Owners agree to inspections by a city inspector, with prior notice so the tenant can be told.
  • A Certificate of Occupancy is withheld until noted problems are repaired and the unit is re-inspected.

Inspectors look for junk cars, dead vegetation, accumulated debris, landscaping, building maintenance, graffiti, adequate refuse facilities, unpermitted construction, dilapidated structures and substandard housing conditions. If you are selling a house you rent, you want those items cleared and your registration current, because a buyer who plans to keep the tenant inherits the compliance duty.

Clinton created an Environmental Court to move code enforcement cases faster than the regular municipal court could. The city says it deals with derelict properties, tree ordinance violations, vandalism, building and fire code violations and other property maintenance matters on private, commercial and residential property.

The city's page quotes the mayor saying such cases sometimes took six months to resolve and that a problem property could face a cycle of citation after citation. The city also notes that Gulfport, Hattiesburg and Biloxi run environmental courts.

An unkept vacant house is the type of property that ends up there. Complaints can be submitted through the city's request form, and Community Development, located at 961 Highway 80 East, handles inspections. If you own a vacant inherited house in Clinton, an open case against it complicates both a listing and a financed sale.

sections.h2: How do Hinds County property taxes work for a Clinton seller?
sections.html:
Taxes on real property in Hinds County are due on or before February 1 for property assessed the previous year. The Hinds County Tax Assessor lists values, the Tax Collector bills and collects, and the Chancery Clerk sends the assessor each recorded deed so that ownership on the roll stays current.

Ownership is set as of January 1, because assessment rolls are prepared annually and local taxes are levied on ownership as of that date. The assessor presents the roll to the Board of Supervisors by the first Monday in July, and the state's normal appeal deadline is the first Monday in August.

  • The assessor's office reviews 25 percent of taxable property every year, so each parcel is inspected at least once every four years.
  • For most homes, the review is a drive-by, and the appraiser contacts the owner only when what is observed differs from the file.
  • Appraisal notices have historically gone out when a value rises by $2,000 or more, and for new assessments.
  • Interior inspections of residences are not required, per the state Department of Revenue.

Hinds County has two judicial districts, and each has its own tax collector and assessor office. The First Judicial District office is in Jackson at 316 S. President Street, and the Second Judicial District office is in Raymond at 127 W. Main Street. Ask which office handles your parcel before you call. You can read the Hinds County Tax Assessor page for the appeal process.

sections.h2: What should a Clinton seller know about the deed and who may draft it?
sections.html:
A deed must be recorded with the Chancery Clerk, and Mississippi limits who may prepare one. The Mississippi Chancery Clerks' Association notes that writing a deed of conveyance for a fee counts as the practice of law under Miss. Code Ann. 73-3-55, and it cites a 1966 state case in which a clerk was found to have engaged in the unauthorized practice of law by drafting deeds.

Recording standards are specific. The same page says instruments need the preparer's name, address and telephone number, and an attorney-prepared instrument must include the attorney's Mississippi Bar number. Hinds County is among the counties that collect the $1.00 archive fee, so the usual charge is $26.00 for a deed, including indexing for the first five pages.

The state disclosure statute applies as well. Under Section 89-1-503, if a seller delivers the property condition statement after an offer is made, the buyer may withdraw within three days of personal delivery or five days of mailing.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale a fit for a Clinton house?
sections.html:
A cash sale can fit when the house has code problems, a tenant or a repair list that would delay a conventional closing. Cash Home Buyers reviews Clinton houses in their current condition, including homes with open code notices, so owners are not required to finish repairs before an offer.

A cash sale does not skip the legal steps. Expect a contract, a title search, a deed prepared by a Mississippi attorney or title company, and recording in the Hinds County land records. Before choosing any route, compare an as-is offer against the cost and time of fixing the house and listing it.

faqs.q: Does Clinton require rental properties to be registered?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's Rental Property Ordinance requires registration of all rental property, annual registration for each unit, and an inspection before a rental license is valid. It covers single-family houses, multifamily units and manufactured homes.

faqs.q: What happens if my Clinton house has a code violation?
faqs.a: The city sends an inspection report that lists the problems and gives a date for compliance. Persistent cases can go to Clinton's Environmental Court, which handles derelict properties, tree ordinance violations and building and fire code violations.

faqs.q: When are Hinds County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due on or before February 1 for property assessed the year before. The Mississippi Department of Revenue adds that if February 1 falls on a weekend or legal holiday, payment the next Monday avoids penalties and interest.

faqs.q: Who can draft a deed in Mississippi?
faqs.a: A Mississippi attorney, typically through a closing attorney or title company. Under Miss. Code Ann. 73-3-55, writing a deed of conveyance for a fee is the practice of law, so a deed should not be prepared by an unlicensed person.

faqs.q: Which Hinds County office serves Clinton property?
faqs.a: Hinds County has First and Second Judicial District offices, in Jackson and Raymond. Confirm with the Tax Assessor or Tax Collector which office handles your parcel before you call.

faqs.q: Do I need to disclose a tornado repair when I sell?
faqs.a: The Mississippi disclosure statement covers the condition of the property, and a seller who delivers it late gives the buyer a right to cancel. Keep records of repairs and insurance claims, and ask a Mississippi real estate attorney how to answer specific questions.
